questions.stem: How many stages can a Fabric deployment pipeline have?

options.text: Exactly 2
Exactly 3
Any number from 1 to 100
From 2 to 10

questions.explanation: A pipeline has three stages by default (Development, Test, Production), and you can set from two to ten when you create it.

questions.stem: The Test and Production stages must read from different lakehouses than Development. What do you set up?

options.text: A separate deployment pipeline for each lakehouse
A shortcut from Production to Development
Deployment rules on the stages, or parameters the rules change per stage
Manual edits in Production after each deployment

questions.explanation: Deployment rules change item settings such as data sources or parameter values when content is deployed to a stage, so each stage points at its own data.

questions.stem: How are deployment pipeline stages related to workspaces?

options.text: Stages don't use workspaces
Each stage is assigned one workspace
A stage can hold several workspaces
All stages share one workspace

questions.explanation: Each stage of a deployment pipeline is backed by one workspace, and deploying copies content from one stage's workspace to the next.

questions.stem: At Harbor Health, a lakehouse is deployed from Test to Production. What arrives in Production?

options.text: Only the data, not the item
The lakehouse item, without the Test lakehouse's table data
A shortcut to the Test lakehouse
The lakehouse with a full copy of Test's data

questions.explanation: Deployment pipelines copy item definitions and metadata, not lakehouse data. Production's lakehouse is loaded by its own pipelines.

questions.stem: You deploy a lakehouse and a semantic model from Test to Production. Which two are not copied to Production? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Item relationships
The data
Permissions on the workspace or items
Model metadata
Parameters

questions.explanation: Deployment copies metadata such as model metadata, parameters and relationships. Data and permissions stay behind.

questions.stem: A pipeline admin must deploy items from Test to Production. What workspace access do they need?

options.text: Contributor or higher on both the source and target workspaces
Admin on the target workspace only
None; being pipeline admin is enough
Viewer on both workspaces

questions.explanation: Deploying requires pipeline admin plus at least Contributor on the workspaces of both stages. A pipeline admin without workspace roles can't deploy.

questions.stem: Where do you create a deployment rule so that a semantic model in Production uses the production data source?

options.text: On the Development stage, so it travels with the model
On the Production stage, then deploy to Production
On the deployment pipeline's settings page, for all stages
In the Git repository's branch policy

questions.explanation: Rules are defined on the target stage and take effect the next time you deploy to it. They can't be created in the development stage.

questions.stem: After deployment, a notebook in Test still uses the Development lakehouse as its default. Which deployment rule fixes this?

options.text: A data source rule on the lakehouse
A default lakehouse rule on the notebook in the Test stage
A data source rule on the notebook
A parameter rule on the notebook

questions.explanation: Notebooks support default lakehouse rules, which set the lakehouse the notebook uses in the target stage. Data source and parameter rules aren't available for notebooks.

questions.stem: A report named Sales was created separately in both the Dev and Test workspaces after they were assigned to the pipeline, so the two aren't paired. What happens when you deploy Sales from Dev to Test?

options.text: The deployment fails with a name conflict
Nothing is deployed
A duplicate copy is created in Test and paired with the Dev report
It overwrites the Test report because the names match

questions.explanation: Only paired items overwrite each other. An unpaired item with the same name results in a new copy that is paired with the source item.

questions.stem: You select a single report for deployment, but it depends on a semantic model that doesn't exist in the target stage. How do you avoid a failed deployment?

options.text: Deploy backward first
Create a deployment rule on the report
Use Select related to add the items it depends on
Turn on autobinding in the pipeline settings

questions.explanation: Select related adds the items that provide dependencies. Without them the deployment fails because the linked item isn't in the target stage.
